lamgods.name: Ghent Altarpiece
lamgods.slogan: The Lamb of God, and one panel that vanished in 1934.
lamgods.line: Completed in 1432, it lost its Just Judges panel to thieves in 1934, and that panel has never been found.

gravensteen.name: Gravensteen
gravensteen.slogan: A count's fortress in the middle of the shopping streets.
gravensteen.line: Built in 1180 by Philip of Alsace, it later served as a mint, a prison and a cotton mill.

rabot.name: Rabot
rabot.slogan: Two stubby towers guarding the water gate of old Ghent.
rabot.line: Built in 1489–1491, its twin towers guarded the lock where the Lieve canal entered the city.

baafsabdij.name: St Bavo's Abbey
baafsabdij.slogan: Cloister ruins that an emperor built a fortress over.
baafsabdij.line: Charles V, born in Ghent, had the abbey destroyed in 1540 and built a fortress with cannons aimed at the city.

boekentoren.name: Book Tower
boekentoren.slogan: Ghent's fourth tower, built for books.
boekentoren.line: Henry van de Velde's 64-metre university library took from 1936 to 1942 to build.
